title: Continuous (Integral) Chebyshev Sum Inequality for Monotone Functions
description: The continuous analogue of Chebyshev's sum inequality: for f, g monotone the same way on [a,b], (∫f)(∫g) ≤ (b−a)∫fg, with the inequality reversing when one is increasing and the other decreasing. Proved from the symmetrised double integral ∫∫(f x−f y)(g x−g y) ≥ 0 via the product measure and Fubini, filling a gap Mathlib leaves open (it has only the discrete sum version).

meta.author: Classical (Chebyshev); formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib

originalContributions: chebyshev_integral_monotoneOn_setIntegral / chebyshev_integral_monotoneOn: the classical monotone-functions-on-an-interval Chebyshev inequality (∫f)(∫g) ≤ (b−a)∫fg for MonotoneOn f, g on Icc a b, stated with the interval integral ∫ x in a..b — the precise continuous analogue of the parent's monotone-sequence form, and the form the gallery's general comonotone entry (oq-01-oq-01-oq-01) does NOT directly provide (that one needs global comonotonicity + boundedness + measurability)
chebyshev_integral_antitoneOn_setIntegral / chebyshev_integral_antitoneOn: the reversed inequality (b−a)∫fg ≤ (∫f)(∫g) for f monotone, g antitone, derived by applying the monotone case to f and −g

The key bridge new over the general entry: integrability of f, g, f·g discharged purely from MonotoneOn (no boundedness assumed) and the comonotone sign transported to the square [a,b]² via Measure.prod_restrict — so the user supplies only monotonicity
sub_mul_sub_nonneg_of_monotoneOn: the pointwise rearrangement sign lemma; norm_le_of_monotoneOn: monotone ⇒ bounded on the interval. Mathlib still has no integral Chebyshev inequality of any form.

overview.historicalContext: Chebyshev's sum inequality is attributed to Pafnuty Chebyshev (1821–1894), who used such 'similarly-ordered' estimates in his work on integration and approximation in the 1880s. In its discrete form it states that for sequences sorted the same way, n·∑aᵢbᵢ ≥ (∑aᵢ)(∑bᵢ): similarly ordered quantities are positively correlated, so their average product exceeds the product of their averages. The continuous (integral) analogue (∫f)(∫g) ≤ (b−a)∫fg for monotone f, g is classical and is treated, for example, in Hardy, Littlewood & Pólya's *Inequalities* (1934), §2.17. It is the simplest instance of a 'correlation inequality': it sits beneath the FKG inequality, the rearrangement inequality, and Chebyshev's integral correlation bound in probability, and it is the deterministic shadow of the covariance fact Cov(f(X), g(X)) ≥ 0 for monotone f, g of a single random variable. Despite this pedigree, Mathlib formalises only the discrete sum version (via its MonovaryOn machinery); the integral form proved here fills that gap.
overview.problemStatement: Chebyshev's sum inequality for finite sequences states that if a₁≤…≤aₙ and b₁≤…≤bₙ are sorted the same way then (∑aᵢ)(∑bᵢ) ≤ n·∑aᵢbᵢ. The parent entry formalises this discrete form via Mathlib's MonovaryOn machinery and poses, as an open question, its continuous counterpart: for monotone functions f, g on an interval [a,b], does (∫ₐᵇ f)(∫ₐᵇ g) ≤ (b−a)∫ₐᵇ f·g hold (reversing for opposite monotonicity)? Mathlib has no integral version of Chebyshev's inequality.
overview.proofStrategy: The whole inequality is the nonnegativity of a single symmetrised double integral `∫∫(f x − f y)(g x − g y) d(μ×μ)`. Monotonicity supplies both ingredients at once: the integrand is pointwise `≥ 0` (the two factors flip sign together) and each monotone function is automatically integrable on the finite-measure interval (`MonotoneOn.integrableOn`). Expanding the product over the product measure and applying Fubini gives `2(b−a)∫fg − 2(∫f)(∫g) ≥ 0`, where the `(b−a)` factor is exactly the total mass of `volume.restrict (Icc a b)`. The reverse inequality for opposite monotonicity needs no separate proof — apply the result to `(f, −g)` and use `∫(−g) = −∫g`.
overview.keyInsight: The continuous inequality is the integral of a manifestly nonnegative two-variable function. Because (f x − f y) and (g x − g y) always share their sign when f and g are monotone the same way, the symmetrised integrand (f x − f y)(g x − g y) is everywhere ≥ 0 on the square [a,b]². Integrating it against the product measure and expanding gives exactly 2(b−a)∫f·g − 2(∫f)(∫g), so nonnegativity of the integral IS the inequality. No continuity is needed — monotone functions are automatically integrable on a finite interval.
keyInsights: The whole inequality is the nonnegativity of a single symmetrised double integral: ∫∫(f x − f y)(g x − g y) d(μ×μ) = 2(b−a)∫fg − 2(∫f)(∫g) ≥ 0. The two-variable integrand makes the 'positive correlation' content manifest before any measure theory is invoked.

Monotonicity alone supplies everything: the pointwise sign (both factors flip together) AND integrability (a monotone function on a finite-measure interval is automatically integrable, MonotoneOn.integrableOn_of_measure_ne_top) — so the theorem needs no continuity or boundedness hypothesis on f, g.

The (b−a) factor is not ad hoc — it is the total mass of the measure volume.restrict (Icc a b). The two diagonal terms of the expansion each contribute (b−a)∫fg (via integral_fun_fst/snd, mass × integral), while the two cross terms each give (∫f)(∫g) (via integral_prod_mul = Fubini).

The reverse inequality for opposite monotonicity is not a separate proof: applying the monotone result to (f, −g) and using ∫(−g) = −∫g flips the sign, since −g is monotone exactly when g is antitone.

This is the continuous shadow of a probabilistic fact: for a single random variable X uniform on [a,b], the inequality is exactly Cov(f(X), g(X)) ≥ 0 for monotone f, g — Chebyshev's integral correlation bound, the 1-dimensional ancestor of the FKG inequality.

It is genuinely sharper-scoped than the gallery's general comonotone entry: that one assumes global comonotonicity, boundedness, and measurability, whereas here the user supplies only MonotoneOn on the interval and gets the familiar interval-integral packaging ∫ x in a..b.
overview.approach: Work with μ = volume.restrict (Icc a b), a finite measure of total mass b−a. Establish integrability of f, g (MonotoneOn.integrableOn_of_measure_ne_top) and of f·g (bounded × integrable). On the product μ.prod μ, expand (f x−f y)(g x−g y) into four product terms; evaluate the two diagonal terms with integral_fun_fst / integral_fun_snd (each contributing (b−a)∫f·g) and the two cross terms with integral_prod_mul (each (∫f)(∫g)). Pointwise nonnegativity of the integrand, transported to the square via Measure.prod_restrict, gives ∫∫ ≥ 0 and hence the inequality. The reverse inequality follows by applying the result to f and −g.
overview.significance: Gives the classical monotone-on-an-interval continuous Chebyshev inequality — the form a reader of the monotone-sequence parent expects — which the gallery's existing general comonotone integral entry does not directly yield (it assumes global comonotonicity, boundedness, and measurability). The contribution is the bridge from MonotoneOn to integrability and the comonotone sign, plus interval-integral packaging. Mathlib has no integral Chebyshev inequality of any kind.
prerequisites: monotone functions are measurable and integrable on bounded intervals

sections.title: Overview: the continuous Chebyshev sum inequality
sections.summary: Module docstring: states the continuous analogue (∫f)(∫g) ≤ (b−a)∫fg of the parent's discrete Chebyshev inequality, contrasts it with the gallery's existing general comonotone entry (which needs global comonotonicity, boundedness, and measurability rather than a local MonotoneOn hypothesis), and outlines the symmetrised-double-integral / Fubini method and its Mathlib ingredients.

sections.title: Pointwise sign of the symmetrised integrand
sections.summary: Opens MeasureTheory/Set, declares the ChebyshevIntegralMonotone namespace and the section variables a b f g. sub_mul_sub_nonneg_of_monotoneOn: for x, y ∈ Icc a b, 0 ≤ (f x − f y)(g x − g y), by case-splitting on x ≤ y vs y ≤ x — both factors are ≤ 0 in one case and ≥ 0 in the other. norm_le_of_monotoneOn bounds a monotone function on [a,b] by max|f a||f b|, used to make f·g integrable.
sections.mathContext: $0 \le (f(x)-f(y))(g(x)-g(y))$ when $f,g$ are monotone the same way.

sections.title: The Fubini identity and the main inequality
sections.summary: chebyshev_integral_monotoneOn_setIntegral. After the degenerate a=b case, sets μ = volume.restrict (Icc a b) (mass b−a), proves integrability of f, g, f·g and of the four product cross-terms, then shows ∫∫(f x−f y)(g x−g y) d(μ×μ) = 2(b−a)∫fg − 2(∫f)(∫g) via integral_prod_mul / integral_fun_fst / integral_fun_snd; nonnegativity of the integrand (transported to the square [a,b]² via Measure.prod_restrict) closes the theorem.

sections.title: Reverse inequality for opposite monotonicity
sections.summary: chebyshev_integral_antitoneOn_setIntegral: with f monotone and g antitone, −g is monotone, so the main theorem applied to (f, −g) and simplified with mul_neg / integral_neg yields the reversed bound (b−a)∫fg ≤ (∫f)(∫g).

sections.title: Interval-integral statements
sections.summary: chebyshev_integral_monotoneOn and chebyshev_integral_antitoneOn restate both the monotone and the reversed antitone inequalities with the familiar interval integral ∫ x in a..b, obtained from the set-integral forms via integral_of_le and integral_Icc_eq_integral_Ioc (Icc and Ioc agree up to a null set).
sections.mathContext: $\big(\int_a^b f\big)\big(\int_a^b g\big) \le (b-a)\int_a^b f\cdot g$, and its antitone reverse $(b-a)\int_a^b fg \le \big(\int_a^b f\big)\big(\int_a^b g\big)$.

conclusion.summary: The continuous Chebyshev sum inequality and its reverse are fully formalised for monotone/antitone functions on a bounded interval, with no axioms or sorries and no continuity hypothesis. The single nonnegative double integral ∫∫(f x−f y)(g x−g y) carries the entire argument; Mathlib's product-integral lemmas evaluate it in closed form.
conclusion.implications: Beyond completing the discrete→continuous pair for Chebyshev's inequality, the result packages a reusable bridge from MonotoneOn to integrability-plus-comonotone-sign that other integral correlation inequalities can reuse. As the 1-dimensional, deterministic case of the FKG/correlation hierarchy, it gives a clean entry point for formalising Cov(f(X),g(X)) ≥ 0 for monotone f, g, and for the rearrangement-inequality circle of results. It also pinpoints exactly what Mathlib lacks (any integral Chebyshev inequality), making it a natural upstream-contribution candidate.
conclusion.futureWork: Sharpen to an equality/rigidity statement (when does equality hold?), or extend to a general finite measure space with a measurable order-correlation hypothesis (a continuous analogue of MonovaryOn).
openQuestions: Characterise the equality case: (∫f)(∫g) = (b−a)∫fg holds iff f or g is a.e. constant on [a,b] — formalise this rigidity statement.
Generalise from Lebesgue measure on [a,b] to an arbitrary finite measure μ with a measurable order-correlation (comonotonicity) hypothesis — a continuous analogue of Mathlib's MonovaryOn.
Derive the probabilistic corollary Cov(f(X), g(X)) ≥ 0 for monotone f, g and X uniform on [a,b], and connect it to the FKG inequality.
Package the MonotoneOn ⇒ integrability + comonotone-sign bridge as a standalone lemma and propose the integral Chebyshev inequality for upstream inclusion in Mathlib.
